title: Count Hills and Valleys in an Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, identify indices that form hills or valleys.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, identify indices that form hills or valleys. An index is a hill if its closest non-equal neighbors are smaller, and a valley if those neighbors are larger. Adjacent indices with the same value are considered part of the same hill or valley. Hills and valleys are counted based on these criteria, excluding indices without non-equal neighbors on both sides.
constraints: For an index, compare the closest value on each side that differs from nums[i].
Equal adjacent values form one plateau and must be counted at most once.
A hill is greater than both non-equal neighbors; a valley is smaller than both.
hints: Plateaus obscure closest non-equal neighbors, so compress consecutive duplicates first.
In the compressed list, every internal local extremum represents exactly one hill or valley.
Both differences share a sign exactly when current is above both neighbors or below both; compression prevents duplicate plateau counts.
editorial: Both differences share a sign exactly when current is above both neighbors or below both; compression prevents duplicate plateau counts.

tests.explanation: After compressing the plateau, four is a hill, one a valley, and six a hill, giving three.
The compressed values decrease monotonically, so there are no hills or valleys.
